newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Jatiya Party chairman Hossain Mohammad Ershad has urged Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to hold trial for corruption committed during the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) regime.

The World Bank has said the country needs to address some generic problems to improve its poor performance in project implementation and suggested that an effective monitoring system should be ensured.

Deputy leader of the opposition BNP, Porfessor A.Q.M. Badruddoza Chowdhury, has said that the Awami League government's initiative to form a new sub-regional forum has been aimed at destroying the SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation).
Bangladesh Small Investors Federation (BSIF) yesterday said the capital market had slightly recovered over the past few days and sought cooperation from all quarters to help sustain this trend.
Bangladesh will face serious food crisis in the next 10 to 15 years unless there is further technological breakthrough in rice production.
Kerb traders have urged the government to establish the National Stock Exchange immediately, failing which they will "set up alternative trading floor" alongside the Dhaka bourse.

Bangladesh's bright prospect of export to Nepal has been thwarted greatly due to lack of road transport facilities. India, the neighbouring country which encircles both Bangladesh and Nepal, has repeatedly refused to give the road permission on security grounds.
Foreign ships at the outer anchorage of the Chittagong port are being targeted by organised gangs of pirates.
